summary: Initial POC scoping call. Goal: define success criteria, workload sizing, timeline, and shortlist open models to evaluate for Solstice's multilingual analytics assistant. Key constraints: data residency, SOC2, p95 latency target ~300-400ms for short responses, domain accuracy for finance analytics, and budget-conscious cost per 1k tokens. Redwood to share POC plan and run benchmarks on 2-3 candidate open models (Mistral-7B, Llama-2-13B, Falcon-40B) with quantization options and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.
topics: Deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Solstice - Head of ML), Tom Bennett (Platform Eng), Elena Ortiz (Data Privacy), Samir Patel (PM)

[00:00] Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — Avery Chen, I'll be your AE. Marco from our SE team is with me. How's everyone?
[00:08] Priya (Solstice): Hi, thanks. Priya here. We are excited to scope the POC, we want to validate open models for our analytics assistant.
[00:14] Marco (Redwood): Great. High level: we'll scope success criteria, workload profile, and pick a short list of open models to benchmark, plus deployment options.
[00:25] Samir (Solstice): Quick context: Solstice builds a multi-lingual analytics chat that ingests proprietary financial datasets. Primary concerns are factual accuracy on domain queries, latency for small responses (< 350ms p95 ideally), and cost per 1k tokens. Also we have data residency rules — EU-only for some customers.
[00:44] Tom (Solstice): From infra, we expect about 3k daily active users at launch, spiky traffic with peak concurrency around ~40-60 RPS for short queries, average sequence length ~250 tokens, but some long analysis prompts up to 2k tokens.
[01:05] Marco: Helpful — that's a good range. For POC we typically recommend a focused workload: 1) short interactive queries (avg 100-300 tokens), 2) medium analytical prompts (~800 tokens), and 3) a handful of long-run like 2k tokens to validate KV cache/sequence behavior. We'll size throughput and target batch strategies accordingly.
[01:28] Priya: Success criteria — what do you usually see customers put as pass/fail? We care about quality (domain accuracy), latency, and unit cost.
[01:37] Avery: We usually make a three-part success criteria: a) Quality: pass rate on an eval set — e.g., >=85% on domain QA + multilingual coverage (EN/ES/FR), b) Latency: p95 under X ms for short queries (we can propose 300-400ms depending on deployment), c) Cost: cost per 1k tokens under a target (you can give us your target and we will model it).
[02:00] Priya: 85% pass sounds reasonable as a start. For cost target, we are aiming to keep inference cost below $0.30 per 1k tokens across average usage — but open to Redwood's modeling.
[02:12] Marco: Noted. For model shortlist, given multilingual and finance domain need, we suggest evaluating: Mistral-7B (fast and cheap, strong base), Llama-2-13B (popular, good instruction tuning), Falcon-40B (higher quality on some long-context tasks), and MPT-30B or mosaicml variants as optional. We can also try quantized Llama-2-13B-QLoRA variants.
[02:41] Tom: Any guidance on which models handle numerical reasoning / finance prompts better?
[02:46] Marco: Generally larger models like Falcon-40B and MPT-30B often do better on complex reasoning, but they cost more. Sometimes a tuned 13B can outperform a generic 40B on narrow domains if you provide an eval set and maybe a small fine-tune or prompt engineering. For POC we'll compare out-of-the-box quality then test small instruction-tuning or retrieval augmentation options.
[03:10] Elena (Data Privacy): For data residency and compliance — we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and KMS support. Also we prefer Private deployment for EU-only workloads. Is that supported?
[03:22] Avery: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem-like deployment with customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit logs. The tradeoff is setup time and cost; Dedicated (reserved capacity) is another middle ground — lower latency variability with isolation. We'll include both in the POC plan and run Hosted first for speed, then a small Dedicated test, and discuss Private if you need EU-only.
[03:44] Samir: Timeline? We need results to decide by mid-January.
[03:48] Avery: Feasible. Proposed timeline: week 1 (this week) finalize success criteria and eval set, week 2 Redwood runs baseline benchmarks on 2-3 models, week 3 we run customer-provided evals and compare qualitative results, week 4 iterate on quantization/tuning and deliver final report. That gets to mid-January.
[04:10] Priya: Sounds good. What metrics will you report in the benchmark?
[04:15] Marco: We'll report: throughput (tokens/s and RPS), latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), cost per 1k tokens (model + infra), memory footprint (GPU RAM), and quality metrics on your eval set (accuracy, F1, multilingual pass rates). We'll also surface model failure modes and hallucination rates on a few gold-standard prompts.
[04:41] Tom: For throughput, can you simulate our spike traffic? We want to know autoscaling behavior.
[04:47] Marco: Yes — we'll run synthetic load with your profile and show batching effects. Redwood's runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache; that will show in throughput numbers. We'll also show how batching impacts tail latency and options to set latency SLOs with lower batch windows.
[05:05] Priya: Model size and quantization — does Redwood support int8 or 4-bit quant?
[05:10] Marco: We support quantized execution paths. For many open models, int8 or 4-bit quantization can cut memory and cost significantly; tradeoffs are small but measurable quality regressions on some tasks. We'll include quantized variants in the baseline.
[05:26] Priya: Multilingual coverage — we need Spanish and French coverage close to English on domain prompts. Which models tend to do that?
[05:33] Marco: Llama-2-13B has decent multilingual, Mistral often does well especially after some prompt engineering, and some Falcon variants are okay. We'll test per-language pass rates. If any model lags, retrieval augmentation (RAG) plus language-specific system prompts help.
[05:51] Samir: Are you able to run benchmarks in our EU region?
[05:55] Avery: Yes — we can run test deployments near your region for latency realism. For Private deployments we'll need some setup. For a Hosted baseline we'll use a nearby region.
[06:06] Tom: Regarding data — will logs or any payload leave our VPC?
[06:09] Elena: This is a hard requirement: customer data must not be stored outside EU for EU-only projects.
[06:15] Avery: For Hosted demo runs we'll avoid sending production data — use synthetic or redacted samples. For Private or Dedicated we can ensure data residency. We'll document KMS and audit capabilities in the security pack we'll share.
[06:30] Priya: For success criteria on quality, can Redwood help build the eval set?
[06:33] Marco: Yes — we can provide a template and tooling; but it's faster if you provide 150-200 domain prompts across languages and annotated gold answers. We'll run automatic metrics plus random manual review.
[06:47] Samir: On cost modeling, can you provide an estimate for avg case and peak?
[06:51] Avery: We'll provide run-rate and peak cost estimates in the POC plan. For rough numbers: a quantized 13B on dedicated infra often sits at significantly lower cost per 1k tokens than a 40B; expect 40B to be ~2-3x the cost depending on batch util. We'll model based on your traffic and 250-token average.
[07:14] Priya: Any recommended first-choice shortlist?
[07:17] Marco: For the POC shortlist we recommend: 1) Mistral-7B (fast baseline, low cost), 2) Llama-2-13B (instruction tuned baseline with good multilingual), 3) Falcon-40B (higher quality on complex finance reasoning). If time permits, run MPT-30B as backup.
[07:33] Tom: Can you quantify expected latencies? p95 numbers per model?
[07:37] Marco: Rough ballpark on typical GPU: Mistral-7B quantized — p95 for short queries could be in 120-220ms range; Llama-2-13B quantized around 200-350ms; Falcon-40B on similar hardware 300-600ms depending on quant and batching. We'll capture exact numbers in the benchmark.
[07:55] Priya: We have some encryption requirements and an internal compliance checklist — will you sign an NDA and provide SOC2 docs?
[08:01] Avery: Yes, we'll share SOC2 report and start an NDA. We'll also send our security pack with KMS and RBAC details. We'll schedule a security deep-dive with Elena.
[08:12] Elena: Also need to know retention policy for logs and audit ability to purge data.
[08:16] Marco: We'll document log retention and purge workflow. For Private/Dedicated you control retention; for Hosted we can set retention options and data deletion processes.
[08:30] Samir: Ok next steps recap?
[08:33] Avery: I'll send the POC plan and benchmark spreadsheet by Monday (2025-12-08). Marco will prepare an internal baseline run and share preliminary numbers. Priya will send the eval prompts. We'll aim to run the first benchmark by 2025-12-12 and reconvene to review results week of 2025-12-15.
[08:52] Priya: Good. Any blockers?
[08:55] Tom: Need service account and VPC connectivity for realistic tests — I'll provision that and share details.
[09:01] Priya: One more question — how do you handle model rollouts and fallback if performance dips?
[09:06] Marco: Redwood supports routing policies and automatic fallback to cheaper or more available model variants. We can set traffic-splitting, canary and A/B rollouts, and fallback rules to Hosted fallback models if Dedicated capacity is constrained. We'll include an example policy in the POC plan.
[09:30] Avery: Alright, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Thanks everyone.
[09:34] Priya: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
